meaning: Number of overseers over the workers at Solomon's temple construction (2 Chron 2:1), and mathematically 60 × 60.
description: The number 3600 appears in 2 Chronicles 2:1, where Solomon appoints 3600 overseers to lead the work of building the temple in Jerusalem. These overseers were responsible for organizing the seventy thousand carriers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains. The figure testifies to the enormous scale of the temple project and the careful administrative organization it required. In the parallel text in 1 Kings 5:30, the number 3300 overseers is mentioned, a difference that has been the subject of rabbinic discussion. Beyond this specific occurrence, the number 3600 does not have a broad symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition, and it plays no known role in gematria.

versions.meaning: The number 3600 has no prominent or well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: The number 3600 does not appear as a symbolically significant number in the Bible or in classical Jewish literature. It can be understood mathematically as 60 × 60, and the number 60 holds some significance in Mesopotamian number systems (the sexagesimal system), but this belongs more to Babylonian than biblical tradition. In Jewish numerology (gematria) there is also no known central connection to this number. If interpretations exist, they are marginal and not part of mainstream biblical or rabbinic symbolism.

footnotes.text: Mathematically, 3600 = 60 × 60. The number 60 was the base in the Mesopotamian sexagesimal system, which was developed in Babylon and influenced among other things timekeeping (60 seconds, 60 minutes). However, this connection belongs more to Babylonian than biblical understanding of numbers.

The difference between 3600 overseers in 2 Chronicles 2:1 and 3300 in 1 Kings 5:30 has been explained in rabbinic tradition as the Books of Chronicles including an additional category of senior leaders that the Books of Kings count separately.
